Secession

/sih-SESH-un/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Secession means the formal act of withdrawing from a political union, federation, or organization.

The mountain province threatened secession after the capital ignored its demands for a full decade.

Worked Example

When the six wealthiest clubs announced their secession from the national league to form a rival competition, fans of the smaller teams felt betrayed.

The clubs did not simply quit playing — they formally withdrew from an organization they belonged to in order to run their own. That organized, declared break is what secession names.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

breakaway: A breakaway is a splitting-off to form something new — a breakaway league, a breakaway faction — and the word often names the offshoot itself. Secession is the formal act of withdrawing from a political union, usually by vote or declaration. Every secession produces a breakaway; breakaway names the offshoot, secession the declared break.

split: A split is any division or falling-out — bands split, parties split, alliances split — and the word says nothing about how it happened. Secession is one specific, procedural kind of break: a member formally withdraws from a union or federation by declared act. Splits can be mutual and messy; a secession is one side's formal departure.

exit: An exit is the plain, neutral word for leaving any arrangement — a company's exit from a market, a country's exit from a treaty. Secession raises the stakes and the formality: a member declares its break from a political union, typically to rule itself afterward. Exits can be quiet; secessions redraw maps.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unification: joining separate parts into one body

accession: formally joining a union or agreement

Where it sits · how confrontational the break becomes — withdrawal → secession → rebellion

withdrawal vs. secession: Withdrawal is milder than secession: a member can quietly withdraw from a committee without any formal, public break.

rebellion vs. secession: Rebellion is stronger than secession: rebels take up arms to overthrow a government, while a seceding region formally votes to leave it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — se-

Prefix — se-: apart, away

Root — cess

Root — cess: to go (Latin cedere, cessus)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or process of

Put it together

Put it together: From Latin secedere: se- (apart) + cedere (to go) + -ion (act of) — the act of going apart, of formally walking away from a union.

Use the root in a new word: concede

Use the root in a new word: concede: After the final votes were counted, the senator phoned her rival to concede the race.

Word Choice

Formal / political-historical

Secession is the formal, declared break of a member from a union — a province from a federation, a chapter from a league — usually with the goal of governing itself afterward. The verb is secede. Watch the sound-alike succession, which means inheriting a position or a series of things in order: one letter apart, entirely different meanings.
